+++ b/.claude/data/floor.yaml
@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@
+# .claude/data/floor.yaml — the one tracked floor source (cycle-129 SDD D-9.2, DEC-0166).
+#
+# The floor is the set of guards, config keys and files no profile, knob or
+# cycle task may weaken. Readers:
+#   - .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh and tests/unit/guard-origins.bats: the
+#     `floor: true` rows of .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml equal floor_guards.
+#   - tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats: every floor_files entry (and the corpus
+#     rows named under floor_corpus) is byte-identical to origin/main.
+#   - tests/unit/profile-floor.bats (Sprint 2): profiles.yaml names no floor_keys.
+# Both bats suites pin this file's sha256; an edit fails until the pin is
+# deliberately updated in the same change (see the FLOOR_SHA256 constant).
+schema_version: 1
+
+floor_guards:
+  - fence:FR-1.2b
+  - fence:FR-SZ
+  - fence:FR-SZ-COPY
+  - fence:FR-SZ-DD
+  - fence:FR-SZ-EXTRACT
+  - fence:FR-SZ-INPLACE
+  - fence:FR-SZ-INTERP
+  - fence:FR-SZ-LINK
+  - fence:FR-SZ-REDIR
+  - fence:FR-SZ-TEE
+  - fence:FR-SZ2
+  - fence:FR-SZ2-COPY
+  - fence:FR-SZ2-INPLACE
+  - fence:FR-SZ2-REDIR
+  - fence:FR-SZ2-RM
+  - fence:FR-SZ2-TEE
+  - gate:verdict-derive
+  - gate:adversarial-review-gate
+  - policy:permission-deny-list
+  - policy:verdict-one-way-rule
+  - policy:operator-only-commands
+
+floor_keys:
+  - flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled
+  - flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled
+  - "flatline_protocol.*.companion_voice"
+  - "destructive_command_guard.*"
+  - "implement_gate.*"
+  - hounfour.locality
+
+# Paths whose bytes must not change relative to origin/main during a cycle.
+floor_files:
+  - .claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh
+  - .claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh
+  - .claude/hooks/settings.deny.json
+  - .claude/data/user-invoked-commands.txt
+
+# Fence-corpus rows (by their `rule` field) that must not change relative to
+# origin/main. A trailing `*` is a prefix match.
+floor_corpus:
+  file: tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl
+  rules:
+    - FR-1.2b
+    - "FR-SZ*"
diff --git a/.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml b/.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..981c9652
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml
@@ -0,0 +1,905 @@
+# .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml — the guard origin map (cycle-129 SDD D-1.1, §3.1).
+#
+# The one hand-written input of the guard register. `.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh`
+# enumerates the guards from the repository (hook commands in .claude/settings.json,
+# `# @guard fence:<id>` markers in block-destructive-bash.sh, `# @guard validator:<id>`
+# markers in validate-artifact.sh) and fails (exit 5) when one has no row here, when a
+# row here resolves to nothing, or when a row's origin is empty. It then writes the
+# tracked structural register grimoires/loa/guards.md and the untracked host yield
+# .run/guard-yield.{md,json}. Regenerate after editing: .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --hooks-table
+#
+# Row fields:
+#   id             hook:<path under .claude/hooks> (scripts outside it: hook:scripts/<name>),
+#                  fence:<pattern id>, validator:<type>.<rule>, gate:<name>, policy:<name>;
+#                  ^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$
+#   kind           hook | fence | validator | gate | policy
+#   class          harness (the model cannot override it) | script (a script checks or
+#                  reports) | prose (the model is asked to comply)
+#   status         active | dormant (armed only by the env var named in knob) |
+#                  telemetry (observes and logs, never refuses)
+#   origin         {kind: kf|issue|finding|cycle|design, ref: <non-empty>}; design rows
+#                  cite the commit that added the guard (git log --follow --diff-filter=A)

diff --git a/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh b/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh
index 6b5f6e3e..f9aa8c41 100755
--- a/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh
+++ b/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh
@@ -525,7 +525,8 @@ emit_block() {
       --arg team_member "${LOA_TEAM_MEMBER:-}" \
       --arg pattern_id "$pattern_id" \
       --arg matched "$sanitized_match" \
-      '{ts: $ts, tool: "Bash", command: $cmd, exit_code: 2, cwd: $cwd, model: $model, provider: $provider, trace_id: $trace_id, team_id: $team_id, team_member: $team_member, hook: "block-destructive-bash", action: "block", pattern_id: $pattern_id, matched: $matched}' \
+      --arg replay "${LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY:-}" \
+      '{ts: $ts, tool: "Bash", command: $cmd, exit_code: 2, cwd: $cwd, model: $model, provider: $provider, trace_id: $trace_id, team_id: $team_id, team_member: $team_member, hook: "block-destructive-bash", action: "block", pattern_id: $pattern_id, matched: $matched} + (if $replay == "1" then {replay: true} else {} end)' \
       >> "${LOA_REPO_ROOT:-.}/.run/audit.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
   } 2>/dev/null || true
 
@@ -541,6 +542,7 @@ check_and_block() {
   if echo "$command" | grep -qE "$pattern" 2>/dev/null; then
     local matched
     matched=$(echo "$command" | grep -oE "$pattern" | head -1)
+    # @guard fence:LEGACY
     emit_block "LEGACY" "$matched" "$message"
   fi
 }
@@ -573,11 +575,13 @@ if [[ "$command" == *"push"* ]]; then
   if [[ "$command" == *"--force"* ]] \
      && _match '(^|/|;|&&|\||[[:space:]]|\(|'"'"'|")[[:space:]]*(sudo[[:space:]]+)?git[[:space:]]+push[[:space:]]+.*--force($|[^-])'; then
     matched=$(echo "$command" | grep -oE 'git[[:space:]]+push[[:space:]]+.*--force[^-]?' | head -1)
+    # @guard fence:P2
     emit_block "P2" "$matched" "git push --force detected. Use --force-with-lease for safer force push, or push to a feature branch."
   fi
   if [[ "$command" == *"-f"* ]] \
      && _match '(^|/|;|&&|\||[[:space:]]|\(|'"'"'|")[[:space:]]*(sudo[[:space:]]+)?git[[:space:]]+push[[:space:]]+.*-f($|[[:space:]])'; then
     matched=$(echo "$command" | grep -oE 'git[[:space:]]+push[[:space:]]+.*-f' | head -1)
+    # @guard fence:P2b
     emit_block "P2b" "$matched" "git push -f detected. Use --force-with-lease for safer force push, or push to a feature branch."
   fi
 fi
@@ -590,6 +594,7 @@ fi
 if [[ "$command" == *"reset"* && "$command" == *"--hard"* ]] \
    && _match '(^|/|;|&&|\||[[:space:]]|\(|'"'"'|")[[:space:]]*(sudo[[:space:]]+)?git[[:space:]]+reset[[:space:]]+--hard'; then
   matched=$(echo "$command" | grep -oE 'git[[:space:]]+reset[[:space:]]+--hard[^[:space:]]*' | head -1)
+  # @guard fence:P3
   emit_block "P3" "$matched" "git reset --hard discards uncommitted work. Use 'git stash' to save changes, or 'git reset --soft' to keep them staged."
 fi
 
@@ -612,6 +617,7 @@ if [[ "$command" == *"clean"* ]]; then
 fi
 if [[ "$has_clean_f" == "true" && "$has_clean_n" == "false" ]]; then
   matched=$(echo "$command" | grep -oE 'git[[:space:]]+clean[[:space:]]+-[a-zA-Z]+' | head -1)
+  # @guard fence:P4
   emit_block "P4" "$matched" "git clean -f without dry-run. Run 'git clean -nd' first to preview what would be deleted."

@@ -50,11 +50,15 @@ ## Language
 **Jack in**: To start an autonomous run under run mode; a run that has finished or been stopped for good has jacked out.
 _Aliases_: jack out
 
+**Judgment**: The task kind for work that needs reading and a decision; it ships as prose or a reviewed artifact, and its sprint task line ends with kind: judgment.
+
 **Kaironic**: Stopping at the right moment rather than after a fixed count: an iterative review loop ends when successive passes stop finding material issues.
 _Avoid_: converged
 
 **Karpathy principles**: The four working rules applied on every code-touching turn: think before coding, simplicity first, surgical changes and goal-driven verification.
 
+**Kind counts**: The release-notes line that counts a cycle's sprint tasks by kind (mechanical, judgment and operator), read from the tagged task lines of its sprint plan.
+
 **Known failure**: A recorded degradation with its symptom, the attempts made and a reading guide, consulted before triage so that prior dead ends are not retried.
 _Aliases_: KF
 
@@ -62,6 +66,10 @@ ## Language
 
 **Map epic**: The epic bead that parents an effort's decision tickets, paired with a map document of its destination, decisions so far, fog and exclusions; run mode never implements it.
 
+**Mechanical**: The task kind for work a script could do reliably; it ships as code with tests, and a review flags a mechanical task delivered as prose the model re-executes.
+
+**Operator**: The human who owns the project and its decisions; as a task kind, work that belongs to that human, which a review flags when it was completed unattended without a decision:unblock ticket or a DEC row.
+
 **Round**: One frontier of interview questions asked together and answered together.
 
 **Run mode**: Unattended execution of a sprint plan with a circuit breaker, wrapping implement, review and audit in a loop. Its states are running, halted and jacked out.
@@ -78,4 +86,6 @@ ## Language
 
 **Voice**: The party a decision or finding is attributed to: the operator, the agent, Flatline or dissent.
 
+**Volume ratio**: The release-notes line that sets a cycle's script lines changed against its prose bytes changed and its model calls; the model-call count is local to the host that ran the cycle.
+
 **Zone**: One of the three permission regions of a repository: the System zone holds the framework and is never edited by hand, the State zone is read and written freely, and the App zone needs confirmation before a write.

file.content:
while IFS= read -r spath; do
    [[ -n "$spath" ]] || continue
    case "$spath" in /*|*..*) echo "gate or policy script '$spath' must be a repository-relative path" >> "$ERRORS"; continue ;; esac
    [[ -f "$ROOT/$spath" ]] || echo "gate or policy script $spath does not exist" >> "$ERRORS"
done < <(jq -r '.guards[] | select(.kind == "gate" or .kind == "policy") | .script' <<<"$MAP_JSON")

if [[ -s "$ERRORS" ]]; then
    sed "s/^/$SCRIPT_NAME: /" "$ERRORS" >&2
    exit 5
fi

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- renderers
# Shared cell sanitiser: control characters removed, pipes escaped for GFM tables.
JQ_DEFS='
  def cell: tostring | explode | map(select(. >= 32 and . != 127)) | implode | gsub("\\|"; "\\|");
  def kinds: ["hook", "fence", "validator", "gate", "policy"];
  def regs: if (.registrations // []) | length == 0 then "-" else (.registrations | map("`" + cell + "`") | join(", ")) end;
  def origin_txt: .origin as $o | if ($o.ref | tostring | startswith($o.kind | tostring)) then ($o.ref | tostring) else "\($o.kind) \($o.ref)" end;
  def yesno: if . == true then "yes" else "no" end;
'

render_register() {
    jq -r "$JQ_DEFS"'
      .guards as $g
      | "# Guard register",
        "",
        "<!-- Generated by .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh from .claude/settings.json, the fence and validator markers and .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml. Do not edit by hand: edit the origin map and regenerate (.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --hooks-table); CI runs --check. -->",
        "",
        "Every guard Loa ships, with its class, status, origin, knob and floor flag. Structural only: the 30-day yield of a host is untracked, in `.run/guard-yield.md` and `.run/guard-yield.json` (regenerate with `.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh`). Classes: harness (the model cannot override it), script (a script checks or reports), prose (the model is asked to comply). Status: dormant means armed only by the env var in the knob column; telemetry means it observes and never refuses.",
        "",
        "- guards: \($g | length)",
        "- guards_without_origin: \($g | map(select((.origin.ref // "") == "")) | length)",
        "- dormant: \($g | map(select(.status == "dormant")) | length)",
        "- floor: \($g | map(select(.floor == true)) | length)",
        (kinds[] as $k | ($g | map(select(.kind == $k))) as $rows | select($rows | length > 0)
          | "",
            "## \($k) (\($rows | length))",
            "",
            "| id | class | status | origin | knob | floor | registrations |",
            "|----|-------|--------|--------|------|-------|---------------|",
            ($rows[] | "| \(.id | cell) | \(.class | cell) | \(.status | cell) | \(origin_txt | cell) | \(.knob | cell) | \(.floor | yesno) | \(regs) |"))
    ' <<<"$MAP_JSON"
}

render_hooks_block() {
    jq -r --argjson hooks "$HOOKS_JSON" "$JQ_DEFS"'
      (.guards | map({key: .id, value: .}) | from_entries) as $by
      | "<!-- guard-register:begin -->",
        "<!-- Generated by .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --hooks-table from .claude/settings.json and .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml; do not edit by hand. Full register: grimoires/loa/guards.md -->",
        "| Event | Matcher | Script | Status | Knob | Purpose |",
        "|-------|---------|--------|--------|------|---------|",
        ($hooks[] | . as $h | $by[$h.id] as $r
          | "| \($h.event | cell) | \(if $h.matcher == "" then "(all)" else ($h.matcher | cell) end) | `\(if $h.wrapped then "hook-guard.sh " else "" end)\($h.id | ltrimstr("hook:") | cell)` | \($r.status | cell) | \($r.knob | cell) | \($r.note // "" | cell) |"),
        "<!-- guard-register:end -->"
    ' <<<"$MAP_JSON"
}

# Rewrites the marker block of $HOOKS_REF into $2 (exit 3 when the markers are absent or repeated).
render_hooks_ref() {
    local block="$1" dest="$2" nb ne
    [[ -f "$HOOKS_REF" && -r "$HOOKS_REF" ]] || die 3 "hooks reference not readable: $HOOKS_REF"
    nb="$(grep -c '^<!-- guard-register:begin -->$' "$HOOKS_REF" || true)"
    ne="$(grep -c '^<!-- guard-register:end -->$' "$HOOKS_REF" || true)"
    [[ "$nb" == "1" && "$ne" == "1" ]] \
        || die 3 "$HOOKS_REF needs exactly one <!-- guard-register:begin --> and one <!-- guard-register:end --> line (found $nb and $ne)"
    awk -v blockfile="$block" '
      /^<!-- guard-register:begin -->$/ { while ((getline l < blockfile) > 0) print l; skip = 1; next }
      /^<!-- guard-register:end -->$/ { skip = 0; next }
      !skip { print }
    ' "$HOOKS_REF" > "$dest"
}

# Atomic replace: temp beside the destination, then rename.
install_file() {
    local src="$1" dest="$2" tmp
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
    tmp="$(mktemp "$(dirname "$dest")/.$(basename "$dest").XXXXXX")"
    cat "$src" > "$tmp"
    chmod 0644 "$tmp"
    mv -f "$tmp" "$dest"
}

REGISTER_NEW="$TMPWORK/guards.md"
render_register > "$REGISTER_NEW"
HOOKS_BLOCK="$TMPWORK/hooks-block.md"
render_hooks_block > "$HOOKS_BLOCK"
HOOKS_REF_NEW="$TMPWORK/hooks-reference.md"
N_GUARDS="$(jq '.guards | length' <<<"$MAP_JSON")"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- --check
if (( DO_CHECK )); then
    render_hooks_ref "$HOOKS_BLOCK" "$HOOKS_REF_NEW"
    drift=0
    if [[ ! -f "$OUT" ]] || ! cmp -s "$REGISTER_NEW" "$OUT"; then
        echo "$SCRIPT_NAME: drift: $OUT differs from the generated register" >&2
        diff -u "$OUT" "$REGISTER_NEW" 2>/dev/null | head -20 >&2 || true
        drift=1
    fi
    if ! cmp -s "$HOOKS_REF_NEW" "$HOOKS_REF"; then
        echo "$SCRIPT_NAME: drift: the guard-register table in $HOOKS_REF differs from the generated one" >&2
        diff -u "$HOOKS_REF" "$HOOKS_REF_NEW" 2>/dev/null | head -20 >&2 || true
        drift=1
    fi
    if (( drift )); then
        echo "$SCRIPT_NAME: $REGEN_HINT" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    echo "$SCRIPT_NAME: in sync ($N_GUARDS guards)"
    exit 0
fi

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- yield
SEGMENTS="$TMPWORK/segments"
: > "$SEGMENTS"
for f in "$AUDIT_LOG" "$AUDIT_LOG".*; do
    [[ -e "$f" ]] || continue
    [[ -f "$f" && -r "$f" ]] || die 3 "audit log segment not readable: $f"
    printf '%s\n' "$f" >> "$SEGMENTS"
done
N_SEGMENTS="$(wc -l < "$SEGMENTS" | tr -d ' ')"
ROWS="$TMPWORK/audit.rows"
: > "$ROWS"
if [[ "$N_SEGMENTS" == "0" ]]; then
    warn "no audit log at $AUDIT_LOG (or segments $AUDIT_LOG.*); the yield is empty"
else
    while IFS= read -r f; do cat -- "$f" >> "$ROWS"; printf '\n' >> "$ROWS"; done < "$SEGMENTS"
fi

TMP_PREFIX="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"
TMP_PREFIX="${TMP_PREFIX%/}/"
MAIN_ROOT=""
if common="$(cd "$ROOT" && git rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)"; then
    common="$(cd "$ROOT" && cd "$common" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" || common=""
    case "$common" in */.git) MAIN_ROOT="${common%/.git}" ;; esac
fi

# Heredoc classification: the FR-6 classifier when present (heredoc_nonexec <command>
# returns 0 for a heredoc whose consumer does not execute it), else `<<` presence.
NONEXEC_IDX='null'
if [[ -f "$HEREDOC_LIB" ]] && grep -q '^heredoc_nonexec[[:space:]]*()' "$HEREDOC_LIB"; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    if source "$HEREDOC_LIB" 2>/dev/null && declare -F heredoc_nonexec >/dev/null; then
        IDX_FILE="$TMPWORK/nonexec.idx"
        : > "$IDX_FILE"
        # Same row indexing as the join below: non-blank lines, in order. Commands travel base64-encoded.
        while IFS="$US" read -r idx b64; do
            [[ -n "$idx" ]] || continue
            cmd="$(printf '%s' "$b64" | base64 --decode 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "$b64" | base64 -D 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if heredoc_nonexec "$cmd" 2>/dev/null; then printf '%s\n' "$idx" >> "$IDX_FILE"; fi
        done < <(jq -R -n -r '[inputs | select(test("\\S")) | (try fromjson catch null)] | to_entries[]
                   | select((.value | type) == "object" and .value.action == "block" and ((.value.command // "") | tostring | contains("<<")))
                   | "\(.key)\u001f\(.value.command | tostring | @base64)"' "$ROWS" 2>/dev/null)
        NONEXEC_IDX="$(jq -R -s 'split("\n") | map(select(length > 0) | tonumber)' "$IDX_FILE")"
    fi
fi

YIELD_JSON="$(jq -R -n \
    --argjson map "$MAP_JSON" \
    --argjson hooks "$HOOKS_JSON" \
    --argjson nonexec "$NONEXEC_IDX" \
    --argjson now "$NOW_EPOCH" \
    --argjson win "$WINDOW_DAYS" \
    --argjson segs "$N_SEGMENTS" \
    --argjson burst_rows "$BURST_ROWS" \
    --arg tmp "$TMP_PREFIX" \
    --arg root "$ROOT" \
    --arg mainroot "$MAIN_ROOT" '
  def epoch: (.ts // .timestamp // null) | if type == "string" then (sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) else null end;
  def under($r): . as $c | ($r != "") and ($c == $r or ($c | startswith($r + "/")));
  def minute: (.ts // .timestamp // "") | tostring | .[0:16];
  def replay($burst): (.replay == true)
    or ((.cwd // "") | type == "string" and (startswith($tmp) or contains("/bats-run-") or contains("/bats.") or contains("/evals/results/") or contains("/sandbox/")))
    or (minute | IN($burst[]));
  def outside_repo: (.cwd // "") as $c | ($c | type == "string") and $c != "" and (($c | under($root)) or ($c | under($mainroot)) | not);
  def verbs: ["rm","git","find","dd","mkfs","shred","truncate","kubectl","terraform","aws","gcloud","psql","mysql","DROP","DELETE","TRUNCATE"];
  def destructive_start: (.command // "") | tostring | [splits("(;|&&|\\|\\||\\||\n)")] | map(sub("^\\s+"; "") | (split("\\s+"; null)[0] // "")) | any(.[]; IN(verbs[]));
  def heredoc: if $nonexec == null then ((.command // "") | tostring | contains("<<")) else (._i | IN($nonexec[])) end;
  def prose_class: (.pattern_id // "") | IN("SP-1", "FR-MERGE-2", "FR-2-AMBIGUOUS");
  def likely_fp: heredoc or outside_repo or (prose_class and (destructive_start | not));
  def day: strftime("%Y-%m-%d");
  def origin_txt: .origin as $o | if ($o.ref | tostring | startswith($o.kind | tostring)) then ($o.ref | tostring) else "\($o.kind) \($o.ref)" end;
  ($hooks | map({key: (.rel | split("/") | last | sub("\\.sh$"; "")), value: .id}) | from_entries) as $hookid
  | ($map.guards | map(.id)) as $known
  | [inputs | select(test("\\S")) | (try fromjson catch null)] as $raw
  | ($raw | to_entries | map(.value as $v | if ($v | type) == "object" then ($v + {_i: .key}) else null end)) as $all
  | ($all | map(select(. != null))) as $rows
  | ($rows | length) as $read
  | ($rows | map(select(.action == "block" or .hook == "implement-gate") | . + {_t: epoch})) as $cand
  | ($cand | map(select(._t != null and ._t >= ($now - $win * 86400) and ._t <= ($now + 86400)))) as $inwin
  | ($inwin | map(select(.action == "block" and .replay != true)) | group_by(minute)
     | map(select(length >= $burst_rows) | .[0] | minute)) as $burst
  | ($inwin | map(select(replay($burst) | not))) as $live
  | ($live | map(
      (if .hook == "block-destructive-bash" then
         ["hook:safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"] + (if ((.pattern_id // "") | tostring | test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$")) then ["fence:" + .pattern_id] else [] end)
       elif .hook == "implement-gate" then ["hook:compliance/implement-gate.sh", "gate:implement-gate"]
       elif ((.hook // "") | type) == "string" and $hookid[.hook] != null then [$hookid[.hook]]
       else [] end) as $ids
      | {ids: ($ids | map(select(IN($known[])))),
         block: (.action == "block" or .action == "deny"),
         telemetry: (.action == "telemetry" or .action == "ask"),
         fp: ((.action == "block" or .action == "deny") and likely_fp),
         t: ._t})) as $cls
  | ($cls | map(.ids[]) | unique) as $seen
  | (["hook:safety/block-destructive-bash.sh", "hook:compliance/implement-gate.sh", "gate:implement-gate"]
     + ($map.guards | map(select(.kind == "fence") | .id)) + $seen | unique) as $writers
  | ($map.guards | map(. as $g
      | if ($g.id | IN($writers[])) then
          ($cls | map(select(any(.ids[]; . == $g.id)))) as $mine
          | ($mine | map(select(.block and (.fp | not))) | map(.t) | max) as $last

diff --git a/evals/README.md b/evals/README.md
index 2a17a1b8..1814557a 100644
--- a/evals/README.md
+++ b/evals/README.md
@@ -500,3 +500,33 @@ # arm A on the pre-change prompt tree (a worktree), arm B on the current tree, s
 `compare.sh` refuses a baseline whose `prompt_tree_sha` equals the tree under comparison, whose
 `captured_at_commit` is not a descendant of the suite's `ab.floor_commit`, or whose `corpus_sha256`
 drifted (`evals/tests/recall-baseline-freshness.bats`). Tests: `evals/tests/{execute-agent,eval-recall-grader,implement-discipline-grader,recall-baseline-freshness}.bats`.
+
+## Control arms and the record corpus (cycle-129 FR-2)
+
+Each recall suite pre-registers control arms in `ab.arms` (review: `baseline`, `no_companion`
+(informational), `no_karpathy`, `no_rule_files`; audit: `baseline`, `no_audit_delta`) and the verdict rule
+in `ab.threshold`. `execute-agent.sh` applies an arm (`LOA_EVAL_ARM`) to the sandbox copy only, after
+materialisation and immediately before the executor starts, and fails the trial (exit 2) when a toggle
+cannot take effect; `executor.json` records `arm`, `arm_toggles`, `arm_evidence`, `source_commit`,
+`models_used` and `refusal_fallbacks`. The executor never inherits the calling Claude Code session's
+coupling, and its subagent model is pinned to `EVAL_MODEL`.
+
+The record fixtures `pr-11` … `pr-18` are the round-1 states of sprints 247–254, built by
+`harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh` from `review-prs/record-pairs.tsv` and the `record/cycle-12x-a2a`
+branches. A feedback finding becomes a label only when the fix commit touches the file it cites. Labels
+live in the hidden `review-prs/labels/pr-NN.tsv` (never in the sandbox-copied `pr-NN/`), every drop is
+explained in `labels/pr-NN.dropped.txt`, and hand curation is the data file `labels/curation.tsv`,
+re-applied on every seed. `fix` rows (the hunks the fix commit changed) feed the grader's refuted share
+only. A label file is approved with `seed-corpus-from-record.sh --approve pr-NN --by "<who> <date>"`;
+`run-arms.sh` refuses unapproved fixtures unless `--allow-unapproved`.
+
+```bash

# optional trailing range keeps `file.py:10-14` in one token, and the comma
# list after it (`:776,807`) belongs to the same path. A bare `:N` (or
# `head:N` / `base:N`) not glued to a word binds to the most recent path.
# a range dash is unspaced (`a.sh:12 - 40 rows` is prose, not a range) and
# every number ends at a boundary: no letter or digit, and no hyphen / en dash
# before another digit, after it (dates such as 2026-10-05 / 2026–10–05 never
# parse; an open `:369-...` still cites 369) — sprint-250 review run 2, #13
RNG = r'(\d{1,6})(?:[-–](\d{1,6}))?(?![A-Za-z0-9]|[-–]\d)'
CITE = re.compile(
    r'(?P<path>[A-Za-z0-9_./+()-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,6})[`*)]{0,3}:(?P<first>' + RNG
    + r'(?:[ \t]*,[ \t]*' + RNG + r')*)'
    # head:N / base:N keep the 1.1.0 boundary set ("head:40" binds); the JSON
    # punctuation set, plus a CLOSING backtick (one after a token character:
    # `rows`:40, `"high"`:3), guards only the fully bare :N — an opening
    # backtick (`:7`, (`:212`)) still binds (RG-13) — run 2, #14
    r'|(?:(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:])(?:head|base)|(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:"\'{}\[\]*])(?<![A-Za-z0-9_"\'}\]]`)):(?P<bare>' + RNG + r')')
ONE = re.compile(RNG)
cites = []
last = None
# the trailer is machine output (its counts are read below), never a citation.
# One pattern strips and reads it (tolerant whitespace, line breaks); the body
# may not contain another comment's `<!--` or `-->`, so an unterminated
# `<!-- LOA-VERDICT` strips nothing — sprint-250 review run 2, #15
TRAILER = re.compile(r'<!--\s*LOA-VERDICT\s*(\{(?:(?!<!--|-->).)*\})\s*-->', re.S)
body = TRAILER.sub('', text)

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# run-arms.sh — cycle-129 FR-2 control-arm driver (SDD D-2.3, DEC-0164, DEC-0171)
     4	#
     5	# Runs the declared control arms of one recall suite on a frozen fixture batch
     6	# against a detached git worktree pinned at --source-commit (never the live
     7	# tree), interleaving trials across arms so provider drift spreads evenly.
     8	#
     9	# Usage:
    10	#   run-arms.sh --suite review-recall|audit-recall --arms a,b,c
    11	#               --fixtures pr-01,pr-02,… --trials 3 --source-commit <sha>
    12	#               [--model <id>] [--concurrency 2] [--batch <name>]
    13	#               [--results-dir evals/results/arms] [--retry-wait <s>]
    14	#               [--allow-unapproved] [--dry-run]
    15	#
    16	# Per trial (fixture × arm × trial), in this order:
    17	#   1. the fixture's SHA256SUMS entries (its files, hidden manifest and labels)
    18	#      are verified; a drift stops the batch (state failed, exit 3). The whole
    19	#      corpus is verified once at batch start (digest in MANIFEST.json); each
    20	#      row records the SHA256SUMS digest seen at its trial, so approving another
    21	#      fixture's labels mid-batch is visible and harmless
    22	#   2. evals/harness/sandbox.sh creates the sandbox from the frozen fixture
    23	#   3. execute-agent.sh runs the executor with EVAL_PROMPT_TREE = the pinned
    24	#      worktree, LOA_EVAL_ARM = the arm (toggles hit the sandbox copy only),
    25	#      LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT, EVAL_MODEL
    26	#   4. grade.sh grades it; the row goes to <batch>/<arm>/results.jsonl with
    27	#      arm, trial, source_commit, model_id, seed (null: the CLI route takes
    28	#      none) and run_date; the artifacts go under <batch>/<arm>/artifacts/
    29	#   A trial whose executor fails for a transport reason (timeout, no result
    30	#   event, API error, rate or session limit) is retried once after
    31	#   --retry-wait seconds; a second failure records an error row and the arm
    32	#   ends `partial`. Other executor failures are recorded, not retried.
    33	#
    34	# Layout: <results-dir>/<suite>/<batch>/{MANIFEST.json,STATUS.json,run.log,
    35	#   <arm>/results.jsonl,<arm>/artifacts/…}; <results-dir>/<suite>/STATUS.json
    36	#   aggregates every batch of the suite (the Sprint 2 gate and report.sh
    37	#   --arms read it). STATUS.json: {state: running|complete|partial|failed,
    38	#   per_arm: {<arm>: {trials_done, trials_failed, trials_planned}},
    39	#   source_commit, model_id, started, finished}.
    40	#
    41	# Exit: 0 complete, 1 partial (some trial failed twice; results kept),
    42	#       2 usage / refused before starting, 3 failed (no trial completed, or
    43	#       the corpus drifted mid-run)
    44	#
    45	# Executor: Fable 5.1 (D33, DEC-0164); the default --model is the id the
    46	# local claude CLI accepted on the cycle-129 probe (claude-fable-5-1).
    47	# Tested by evals/tests/run-arms.bats (stubbed CLI; no model call).
    48	# =============================================================================
    49	set -euo pipefail
    50	export LC_ALL=C
    51	
    52	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    53	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    54	EVALS_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/evals"
    55	CORPUS_DIR="$EVALS_DIR/fixtures/review-prs"
    56	DEFAULT_MODEL="claude-fable-5-1"
    57	CACHE_ROOT="${LOA_ARMS_CACHE:-$HOME/.cache/loa/cycle-129}"
    58	# the repository the pinned source worktree is cut from (tests point it at a
    59	# throwaway repo so they never register a worktree in the real one)
    60	SOURCE_REPO="${LOA_ARMS_SOURCE_REPO:-$REPO_ROOT}"
    61	
    62	SUITE="" ARMS_CSV="" FIXTURES_CSV="" TRIALS="" SOURCE_COMMIT="" MODEL="$DEFAULT_MODEL"
    63	CONCURRENCY=2 BATCH="" RESULTS_ROOT="$EVALS_DIR/results/arms" RETRY_WAIT=300
    64	DRY_RUN=false ALLOW_UNAPPROVED=false
    65	
    66	usage() { sed -n '2,/^# =====.*$/p' "$0" | sed -n '2,46p' | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2; }
    67	die() { echo "run-arms: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    68	
    69	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    70	  case "$1" in
    71	    --suite) SUITE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    72	    --arms) ARMS_CSV="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    73	    --fixtures) FIXTURES_CSV="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    74	    --trials) TRIALS="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    75	    --source-commit) SOURCE_COMMIT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    76	    --model) MODEL="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    77	    --concurrency) CONCURRENCY="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    78	    --batch) BATCH="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    79	    --results-dir) RESULTS_ROOT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    80	    --retry-wait) RETRY_WAIT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    81	    --allow-unapproved) ALLOW_UNAPPROVED=true; shift ;;
    82	    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=true; shift ;;
    83	    --help|-h) usage ;;
    84	    *) die "unknown option: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    85	  esac
    86	done
    87	
    88	# --- validate arguments ------------------------------------------------------
    89	case "$SUITE" in review-recall|audit-recall) ;; *) die "--suite must be review-recall or audit-recall" ;; esac
    90	[[ "$TRIALS" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]?$ ]] || die "--trials must be an integer 1-99"
    91	[[ "$CONCURRENCY" =~ ^[1-9]$ ]] || die "--concurrency must be 1-9"
    92	[[ "$RETRY_WAIT" =~ ^[0-9]{1,5}$ ]] || die "--retry-wait must be whole seconds"
    93	[[ "$MODEL" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._:/-]+$ ]] || die "--model has unexpected characters"
    94	[[ "$SOURCE_COMMIT" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$ ]] || die "--source-commit must be a hex commit id"
    95	for tool in git jq yq python3; do command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "missing tool: $tool"; done
    96	
    97	SUITE_FILE="$EVALS_DIR/suites/$SUITE.yaml"
    98	[[ -f "$SUITE_FILE" ]] || die "suite file not found: $SUITE_FILE"
    99	TASK_PREFIX="review"; [[ "$SUITE" == "audit-recall" ]] && TASK_PREFIX="audit"
   100	
   101	IFS=',' read -r -a ARMS <<<"$ARMS_CSV"
   102	IFS=',' read -r -a FIXTURES <<<"$FIXTURES_CSV"
   103	[[ ${#ARMS[@]} -gt 0 && -n "${ARMS[0]}" ]] || die "--arms is required"
   104	[[ ${#FIXTURES[@]} -gt 0 && -n "${FIXTURES[0]}" ]] || die "--fixtures is required"
   105	for a in "${ARMS[@]}"; do
   106	  [[ "$a" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$ ]] || die "invalid arm id '$a'"
   107	  [[ "$(A="$a" yq '[.ab.arms[]? | select(.id == strenv(A))] | length' "$SUITE_FILE")" -gt 0 ]] \
   108	    || die "arm '$a' is not declared in $SUITE_FILE (ab.arms[])"
   109	done
   110	for f in "${FIXTURES[@]}"; do
   111	  [[ "$f" =~ ^pr-[0-9]{2}$ ]] || die "invalid fixture id '$f' (want pr-NN)"
   112	  [[ -d "$CORPUS_DIR/$f" ]] || die "fixture not found: $CORPUS_DIR/$f"
   113	  [[ -f "$CORPUS_DIR/manifests/$f.json" ]] || die "hidden manifest not found for $f"
   114	  [[ -f "$EVALS_DIR/tasks/$SUITE/$TASK_PREFIX-$f.yaml" ]] || die "task not found: tasks/$SUITE/$TASK_PREFIX-$f.yaml"
   115	  if [[ "$(jq -r 'if has("approved") then .approved else true end' "$CORPUS_DIR/manifests/$f.json")" != "true" \
   116	        && "$ALLOW_UNAPPROVED" != "true" ]]; then
   117	    die "$f: labels.tsv is not approved yet (seed-corpus-from-record.sh --approve $f --by '<who> <date>'), or pass --allow-unapproved"
   118	  fi
   119	done
   120	
   121	SRC_FULL="$(git -C "$SOURCE_REPO" rev-parse --verify --quiet "${SOURCE_COMMIT}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null)" \
   122	  || die "source commit $SOURCE_COMMIT is not in this repository"
   123	SRC12="${SRC_FULL:0:12}"
   124	WORKTREE="$CACHE_ROOT/arms-src-$SRC12"
   125	
   126	[[ -n "$BATCH" ]] || BATCH="batch-${FIXTURES[0]}-${FIXTURES[${#FIXTURES[@]}-1]}-n${#FIXTURES[@]}"
   127	[[ "$BATCH" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,80}$ ]] || die "invalid --batch '$BATCH'"
   128	SUITE_DIR="$RESULTS_ROOT/$SUITE"
   129	BATCH_DIR="$SUITE_DIR/$BATCH"
   130	
   131	# --- corpus freeze ------------------------------------------------------------
   132	# verify_corpus [<fixture>] — every SHA256SUMS entry (or one fixture's entries
   133	# and its manifest) hashes as recorded. Prints the SHA256SUMS digest.
   134	verify_corpus() {
   135	  python3 -I - "$CORPUS_DIR" "${1:-}" <<'PY'
   136	import hashlib, os, sys
   137	corpus, only = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   138	sums = os.path.join(corpus, "SHA256SUMS")
   139	raw = open(sums, "rb").read()
   140	bad = []
   141	for line in raw.decode("utf-8").splitlines():
   142	    if not line.strip():
   143	        continue
   144	    digest, rel = line.split("  ", 1)
   145	    if only and not (rel.startswith(only + "/") or rel == f"manifests/{only}.json" or rel == "corpus.tsv"
   146	                     or rel.startswith(f"labels/{only}.")):
   147	        continue
   148	    p = os.path.join(corpus, rel)
   149	    if not os.path.isfile(p) or hashlib.sha256(open(p, "rb").read()).hexdigest() != digest:
   150	        bad.append(rel)
   151	if bad:
   152	    print("corpus drift: " + ", ".join(bad[:10]), file=sys.stderr)
   153	    sys.exit(1)
   154	print(hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest())
   155	PY
   156	}
   157	CORPUS_DIGEST="$(verify_corpus)" || die "fixture corpus does not match SHA256SUMS (run build/seed with --check first)"
   158	
   159	# --- the planned trials (interleaved: trial-major, then fixture, then arm) ----
   160	PLAN=()
   161	for t in $(seq 1 "$TRIALS"); do
   162	  for f in "${FIXTURES[@]}"; do
   163	    for a in "${ARMS[@]}"; do PLAN+=("$a|$f|$t"); done
   164	  done

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# run-arms.sh — cycle-129 FR-2 control-arm driver (SDD D-2.3, DEC-0164, DEC-0171)
     4	#
     5	# Runs the declared control arms of one recall suite on a frozen fixture batch
     6	# against a detached git worktree pinned at --source-commit (never the live
     7	# tree), interleaving trials across arms so provider drift spreads evenly.
     8	#
     9	# Usage:
    10	#   run-arms.sh --suite review-recall|audit-recall --arms a,b,c
    11	#               --fixtures pr-01,pr-02,… --trials 3 --source-commit <sha>
    12	#               [--model <id>] [--concurrency 2] [--batch <name>]
    13	#               [--results-dir evals/results/arms] [--retry-wait <s>]
    14	#               [--allow-unapproved] [--dry-run]
    15	#
    16	# Per trial (fixture × arm × trial), in this order:
    17	#   1. the fixture's SHA256SUMS entries (its files, hidden manifest and labels)
    18	#      are verified; a drift stops the batch (state failed, exit 3). The whole
    19	#      corpus is verified once at batch start (digest in MANIFEST.json); each
    20	#      row records the SHA256SUMS digest seen at its trial, so approving another
    21	#      fixture's labels mid-batch is visible and harmless
    22	#   2. evals/harness/sandbox.sh creates the sandbox from the frozen fixture
    23	#   3. execute-agent.sh runs the executor with EVAL_PROMPT_TREE = the pinned
    24	#      worktree, LOA_EVAL_ARM = the arm (toggles hit the sandbox copy only),
    25	#      LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT, EVAL_MODEL
    26	#   4. grade.sh grades it; the row goes to <batch>/<arm>/results.jsonl with
    27	#      arm, trial, source_commit, model_id, seed (null: the CLI route takes
    28	#      none) and run_date; the artifacts go under <batch>/<arm>/artifacts/
    29	#   A trial whose executor fails for a transport reason (timeout, no result
    30	#   event, API error, rate or session limit) is retried once after
    31	#   --retry-wait seconds; a second failure records an error row and the arm
    32	#   ends `partial`. Other executor failures are recorded, not retried.
    33	#
    34	# Layout: <results-dir>/<suite>/<batch>/{MANIFEST.json,STATUS.json,run.log,
    35	#   <arm>/results.jsonl,<arm>/artifacts/…}; <results-dir>/<suite>/STATUS.json

   132	# verify_corpus [<fixture>] — every SHA256SUMS entry (or one fixture's entries
   133	# and its manifest) hashes as recorded. Prints the SHA256SUMS digest.
   134	verify_corpus() {
   135	  python3 -I - "$CORPUS_DIR" "${1:-}" <<'PY'
   136	import hashlib, os, sys
   137	corpus, only = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   138	sums = os.path.join(corpus, "SHA256SUMS")
   139	raw = open(sums, "rb").read()
   140	bad = []
   141	for line in raw.decode("utf-8").splitlines():
   142	    if not line.strip():
   143	        continue
   144	    digest, rel = line.split("  ", 1)
   145	    if only and not (rel.startswith(only + "/") or rel == f"manifests/{only}.json" or rel == "corpus.tsv"
   146	                     or rel.startswith(f"labels/{only}.")):
   147	        continue
   148	    p = os.path.join(corpus, rel)
   149	    if not os.path.isfile(p) or hashlib.sha256(open(p, "rb").read()).hexdigest() != digest:
   150	        bad.append(rel)
   151	if bad:
   152	    print("corpus drift: " + ", ".join(bad[:10]), file=sys.stderr)
   153	    sys.exit(1)
   154	print(hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest())
   155	PY
   156	}

   283	# The suite-level STATUS.json merges every batch: counters add per arm; the
   284	# state is failed > running > partial > complete; source/model must agree.
   285	aggregate_status() {
   286	  local agg="$SUITE_DIR/STATUS.json" lockd="$SUITE_DIR/.status.lock" n=0
   287	  until mkdir "$lockd" 2>/dev/null; do n=$((n + 1)); [[ $n -gt 50 ]] && return 0; sleep 0.1; done

   291	    (map(.state) | max_by(rank)) as $state |
   292	    {schema_version: 1, suite: $suite, state: $state,
   293	     batches: map({batch, state, started, finished}),
   294	     per_arm: (reduce (.[] | .per_arm | to_entries[]) as $e ({};
   295	        .[$e.key] |= {trials_done: ((.trials_done // 0) + $e.value.trials_done),
   296	                      trials_failed: ((.trials_failed // 0) + $e.value.trials_failed),
   297	                      trials_planned: ((.trials_planned // 0) + $e.value.trials_planned)})),
   298	     source_commit: (map(.source_commit) | unique | if length == 1 then .[0] else "MIXED" end),
   299	     model_id: (map(.model_id) | unique | if length == 1 then .[0] else "MIXED" end),
   300	     started: (map(.started) | min), finished: (if $state == "running" then null else (map(.finished) | max) end)}' \
   301	    $(find "$SUITE_DIR" -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 -name STATUS.json | sort) > "$agg.tmp" 2>/dev/null \

   303	  rmdir "$lockd" 2>/dev/null || true

name: review-recall
description: "cycle-124 FR-9 A/B suite: review-recall (arm A = Sprint-2 tip prompts, arm B = audited prompts; same executor model, fixed effort)"
version: 1

tasks:
  include:
    - "tasks/review-recall/**/*.yaml"
  exclude: []

defaults:
  trials: 3
  timeout:
    per_trial: 1500
    per_grader: 180
  composite_strategy: all_must_pass

# compare.sh freshness rule (evals/tests/recall-baseline-freshness.bats):
# a baseline must be captured at or after floor_commit (the Sprint-2 landing
# commit) on a prompt tree different from the one under comparison, with the
# corpus frozen.

input.command: cd /workspace/pr; awk '/^diff --git a\/evals\/tests\/eval-recall-grader.bats/,/^diff --git a\/evals\/tests\/fixtures\/claude-stub.sh/' head.diff; awk '/^diff --git a\/evals\/tests\/golden-path.bats/,/^diff --git a\/evals\/tests\/run-arms.bats/' head.diff

   [ "$(yq -r '.model_version' "$T/out.yaml")" = "m1" ]
   [ "$(yq -r '.recorded_from_run' "$T/out.yaml")" = "r" ]
 }
+
+# ---- control arms (cycle-129 FR-2, SDD D-2.3) --------------------------------
+
+# Stamp every row of an arm dir with an arm id and per-row source commits.
+stamp_arm() {  # stamp_arm <dir> <arm> <source-row1> [<source-row2>]
+  local d="$1" arm="$2" s1="$3" s2="${4:-$3}"
+  jq -c --arg arm "$arm" --arg s1 "$s1" --arg s2 "$s2" \
+    '. + {arm: $arm, source_commit: (if .task_id == "review-pr-01" then $s1 else $s2 end)}' \
+    "$d/results.jsonl" > "$d/r.tmp" && mv "$d/r.tmp" "$d/results.jsonl"
+}
+
+@test "BF-10 control arms on one pinned source tree compare (the same-tree rule yields to distinct arm ids)" {
+  mk_arm "$T/a" m1 "$TREE_SHA" false 1 0 1000
+  mk_arm "$T/b" m1 "$TREE_SHA" false 1 0 900
+  stamp_arm "$T/a" baseline 864069f2
+  stamp_arm "$T/b" no_rule_files 864069f2
+  run "$COMPARE" --ab --arm-a "$T/a" --arm-b "$T/b" --metric recall --json
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.valid')" = "true" ]
+  [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.arms.b.arm_ids[0]')" = "no_rule_files" ]
+}
+
+@test "BF-11 --ab refuses mixed source_commit values across control arms (exit 2, named reason)" {
+  mk_arm "$T/a" m1 "$TREE_SHA" false 1 0 1000
+  mk_arm "$T/b" m1 "$TREE_SHA" false 1 0 1000
+  stamp_arm "$T/a" baseline 864069f2
+  stamp_arm "$T/b" no_karpathy ffd25258
+  run "$COMPARE" --ab --arm-a "$T/a" --arm-b "$T/b" --metric recall --json
+  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+  echo "$output" | jq -r '.reasons[]' | grep -q 'source commit skew across arms'
+}
+
+@test "BF-12 --ab refuses mixed source_commit values across one arm's trials, and two arm ids in one arm" {
+  mk_arm "$T/a" m1 "$TREE_SHA" false 1 0 1000
+  mk_arm "$T/b" m1 "$TREE_SHA" false 1 0 1000
+  stamp_arm "$T/a" baseline 864069f2 ffd25258
+  stamp_arm "$T/b" no_karpathy 864069f2
+  run "$COMPARE" --ab --arm-a "$T/a" --arm-b "$T/b" --metric recall --json
+  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+  echo "$output" | jq -r '.reasons[]' | grep -q 'source commit skew across trials'
+  mk_arm "$T/a" m1 "$TREE_SHA" false 1 0 1000
+  jq -c '. + {arm: (if .task_id == "review-pr-01" then "baseline" else "no_karpathy" end), source_commit: "864069f2"}' \
+    "$T/a/results.jsonl" > "$T/a/r.tmp" && mv "$T/a/r.tmp" "$T/a/results.jsonl"
+  run "$COMPARE" --ab --arm-a "$T/a" --arm-b "$T/b" --metric recall --json
+  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+  echo "$output" | jq -r '.reasons[]' | grep -q 'mixes arm ids'
+}
+
+@test "BF-13 control arms still refuse executor model skew, and the same arm on both sides is no control comparison" {
+  mk_arm "$T/a" m1 "$TREE_SHA" false 1 0 1000
+  mk_arm "$T/b" m2 "$TREE_SHA" false 1 0 1000
+  stamp_arm "$T/a" baseline 864069f2
+  stamp_arm "$T/b" no_rule_files 864069f2
+  run "$COMPARE" --ab --arm-a "$T/a" --arm-b "$T/b" --metric recall --json
+  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+  echo "$output" | jq -r '.reasons[]' | grep -q 'model id skew'
+  mk_arm "$T/b" m1 "$TREE_SHA" false 1 0 1000
+  stamp_arm "$T/b" baseline 864069f2
+  run "$COMPARE" --ab --arm-a "$T/a" --arm-b "$T/b" --metric recall --json
+  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+  echo "$output" | jq -r '.reasons[]' | grep -q 'same prompt tree'
+}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/cycle-ratio.sh: the two release-notes lines of a cycle, task-kind
     4	# counts and the volume ratio (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-10.3, PRD FR-10).
     5	#
     6	#   kinds: mechanical N · judgment N · operator N
     7	#   volume: script lines changed N (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed N (*.md) · model calls N (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: <path>
     8	#
     9	# Mapping (the glossary's "Kind counts" and "Volume ratio" entries):
    10	#   kinds          the 'kind: <value>' token that ends each top-level '- [ ]' /
    11	#                  '- [x]' task line under '### Technical Tasks', and each
    12	#                  '- [ ] Task ...' line under a '### Task N.E2E' heading, inside
    13	#                  a '## Sprint N' block of the sprint plan (fenced code skipped,
    14	#                  the same scope validate-artifact.sh --type sprint enforces);
    15	#                  untagged task lines are counted in --json and WARNed
    16	#   script lines   added + deleted lines of *.sh *.py *.ts *.js files between
    17	#                  the two commits (git diff --numstat, renames detected,
    18	#                  binary files skipped)
    19	#   prose bytes    bytes of the added and removed *.md lines between the two
    20	#                  commits, newline included, diff markers excluded
    21	#   model calls    MODELINV rows (primitive_id MODELINV) in the MODELINV log
    22	#                  whose ts_utc lies between the two commits' committer
    23	#                  timestamps, both ends included. The log is host-local, so
    24	#                  the count covers only the calls made on this host: "scope:
    25	#                  host". A missing log prints "model calls n/a" and a WARN.
    26	#
    27	# Git runs in the current directory's repository; --sprint-plan and --modelinv
    28	# default to paths under its top level.
    29	#
    30	# Usage:
    31	#   tools/cycle-ratio.sh --from SHA --to SHA [--sprint-plan PATH]
    32	#                        [--modelinv PATH] [--json]
    33	#
    34	#   --sprint-plan PATH  default grimoires/loa/sprint.md
    35	#   --modelinv PATH     default .run/model-invoke.jsonl
    36	#   --json              one JSON object instead of the two lines
    37	#
    38	# Exit 2 also covers: not a git repository, an unreadable sprint plan, jq missing.
    39	# Exit codes: 0 printed · 2 usage or unreadable input · 3 a SHA names no commit
    40	# =============================================================================
    41	set -euo pipefail
    42	export LC_ALL=C
    43	
    44	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    45	die() { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: $2" >&2; exit "$1"; }
    46	
    47	SCRIPT_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
    48	FENCE_AWK="$SCRIPT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/md-fence.awk"
    49	
    50	FROM=""
    51	TO=""
    52	PLAN=""
    53	MODELINV=""
    54	JSON=0
    55	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    56	  case "$1" in
    57	    --from|--to|--sprint-plan|--modelinv)
    58	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: $1 needs a value" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    59	      case "$1" in
    60	        --from) FROM="$2" ;;
    61	        --to) TO="$2" ;;
    62	        --sprint-plan) PLAN="$2" ;;
    63	        --modelinv) MODELINV="$2" ;;
    64	      esac
    65	      shift 2 ;;
    66	    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
    67	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
    68	    *) echo "cycle-ratio.sh: unknown argument $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
    69	  esac
    70	done
    71	
    72	[[ -n "$FROM" && -n "$TO" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: --from and --to are required" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    73	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 2 "jq is required"
    74	TOP="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die 2 "not inside a git repository"
    75	[[ -n "$PLAN" ]] || PLAN="$TOP/grimoires/loa/sprint.md"
    76	[[ -n "$MODELINV" ]] || MODELINV="$TOP/.run/model-invoke.jsonl"
    77	[[ -r "$PLAN" && -f "$PLAN" ]] || die 2 "sprint plan not readable: $PLAN"
    78	[[ -r "$FENCE_AWK" ]] || die 2 "cannot read $FENCE_AWK (reinstall the framework scripts)"
    79	
    80	# A leading '-' would reach git as an option; a SHA never starts with one.
    81	case "$FROM" in -*) die 3 "unknown commit: $FROM" ;; esac
    82	case "$TO" in -*) die 3 "unknown commit: $TO" ;; esac
    83	FROM_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${FROM}^{commit}")" || die 3 "unknown commit: $FROM"
    84	TO_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${TO}^{commit}")" || die 3 "unknown commit: $TO"
    85	
    86	# --- kinds -------------------------------------------------------------------
    87	kinds="$(awk "$(cat "$FENCE_AWK")"'
    88	  md_fence($0) { next }
    89	  /^## / { insp = ($0 ~ /^## Sprint [0-9]/); sec = 0; next }
    90	  !insp { next }
    91	  /^### / {
    92	    sec = 0
    93	    if ($0 ~ /^### Technical Tasks[[:space:]]*$/) sec = 1
    94	    else if ($0 ~ /^### Task [0-9A-Za-z]+\.E2E([^A-Za-z0-9]|$)/) sec = 2
    95	    next
    96	  }
    97	  !sec || $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] / { next }
    98	  sec == 2 && $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] Task / { next }
    99	  {
   100	    if (match($0, /(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])kind[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*(mechanical|judgment|operator)[[:space:]]*$/)) {
   101	      v = substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH)
   102	      sub(/^.*:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", v)
   103	      n[v]++
   104	    } else n["untagged"]++
   105	  }
   106	  END { printf "%d %d %d %d\n", n["mechanical"], n["judgment"], n["operator"], n["untagged"] }
   107	' "$PLAN")"
   108	read -r K_MECH K_JUDG K_OPER K_UNTAGGED <<< "$kinds"
   109	[[ "$K_UNTAGGED" -eq 0 ]] || echo "WARN: $K_UNTAGGED task line(s) in $PLAN carry no kind: tag and are not counted" >&2
   110	
   111	# --- volume ------------------------------------------------------------------
   112	GIT_DIFF=(git -c core.quotePath=false diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv -M)
   113	SCRIPT_LINES="$("${GIT_DIFF[@]}" --numstat "$FROM_SHA" "$TO_SHA" -- '*.sh' '*.py' '*.ts' '*.js' \
   114	  | awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ && $2 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ { s += $1 + $2 } END { printf "%d\n", s }')"
   115	PROSE_BYTES="$("${GIT_DIFF[@]}" --unified=0 "$FROM_SHA" "$TO_SHA" -- '*.md' \
   116	  | awk '
   117	      /^diff --git / { hunk = 0; next }
   118	      /^@@ / { hunk = 1; next }
   119	      # the marker byte stands in for the newline the diff line drops
   120	      hunk && /^[+-]/ { s += length($0) }
   121	      END { printf "%d\n", s }
   122	    ')"
   123	
   124	# --- model calls -------------------------------------------------------------
   125	FROM_TS="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$FROM_SHA")"
   126	TO_TS="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$TO_SHA")"
   127	MODEL_CALLS=""
   128	if [[ -f "$MODELINV" && -r "$MODELINV" ]]; then
   129	  MODEL_CALLS="$(jq -R --argjson lo "$FROM_TS" --argjson hi "$TO_TS" '
   130	      fromjson? | select(type == "object" and .primitive_id == "MODELINV")
   131	      | (.ts_utc // "") | tostring
   132	      | (try (sub("\\.[0-9]+"; "") | sub("\\+00:00$"; "Z") | fromdateiso8601) catch null)
   133	      | select(. != null and . >= $lo and . <= $hi)
   134	    ' "$MODELINV" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
   135	else
   136	  echo "WARN: MODELINV log not found at $MODELINV; model calls n/a" >&2
   137	fi
   138	
   139	iso() { jq -nr --argjson t "$1" '$t | todateiso8601'; }
   140	
   141	if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
   142	  jq -n \
   143	    --arg from "$FROM_SHA" --arg to "$TO_SHA" \
   144	    --arg from_ts "$(iso "$FROM_TS")" --arg to_ts "$(iso "$TO_TS")" \
   145	    --arg plan "$PLAN" --arg modelinv "$MODELINV" \
   146	    --argjson mech "$K_MECH" --argjson judg "$K_JUDG" --argjson oper "$K_OPER" --argjson untagged "$K_UNTAGGED" \
   147	    --argjson script_lines "$SCRIPT_LINES" --argjson prose_bytes "$PROSE_BYTES" \
   148	    --arg calls "$MODEL_CALLS" \
   149	    '{from: $from, to: $to, window: {from: $from_ts, to: $to_ts}, sprint_plan: $plan,
   150	      kinds: {mechanical: $mech, judgment: $judg, operator: $oper, untagged: $untagged},
   151	      volume: {script_lines_changed: $script_lines, prose_bytes_changed: $prose_bytes,
   152	               model_calls: (if $calls == "" then null else ($calls | tonumber) end),
   153	               scope: "host", modelinv: $modelinv}}'
   154	else
   155	  printf 'kinds: mechanical %s · judgment %s · operator %s\n' "$K_MECH" "$K_JUDG" "$K_OPER"
   156	  printf "volume: script lines changed %s (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed %s (*.md) · model calls %s (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: %s\n" \
   157	    "$SCRIPT_LINES" "$PROSE_BYTES" "${MODEL_CALLS:-n/a}" "$MODELINV"
   158	fi

head/tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats:39 — HIGH: FS-2's jq filter does not compile. `def m($r)` reads `$in`, but `$in` is only bound after the def (`. as $in | select(m($rules))`), and jq resolves variables lexically, so it fails with "$in is not defined" (exit 3). Both process substitutions in the `diff` on line 41 then produce empty output, and diff of empty vs empty exits 0. The test passes whatever happens to the FR-1.2b / FR-SZ* fence-corpus rows, so the floor_corpus guard is vacuous. Bind the row before the def, or pass it as an argument (`def m($row; $r)`), and make the test fail when either side is empty.
head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:266 — MEDIUM: when neither stash-safety.md nor skill-invariants.md exists in the sandbox, the rule_files toggle records `removed: none present` and returns success. The arm then runs exactly as its baseline. That breaks the contract stated in the header (execute-agent.sh:63-65) and in the README: a toggle that cannot take effect must exit 2, and an arm never silently runs as its baseline. The karpathy_block and audit_delta_instruction toggles do fail when there is nothing to remove, and AT-9 covers only those two. Fail when `gone` is empty, or at least when either file is missing.
head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:408 — MEDIUM: rerunning a batch that already holds results is allowed (lines 251-256 accept it when source and model match), but collect() only appends to <arm>/results.jsonl and never truncates or dedupes it. A rerun (e.g. after a partial run) doubles every (fixture, arm, trial) row, while the per-batch DONE/FAILED counters restart at 0. arms-report.py pools every row, so coverage_gaps reads 6/3 trials and trial_means merges two runs under the same trial number. The pre-registered verdict is then computed on mixed, double-counted data. Either refuse a non-dry-run reuse of a batch that has results, or replace or skip rows already present.
head/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md:2 — MEDIUM: the new path scope (`**/*.sh`, `**/*.bats`, `.claude/scripts/**`, `.claude/hooks/**`) loads the stash rule only when shell sources are touched. The hazard is a git stash run from Bash during any skill. The incident the rule cites (#555, line 39) lost Edit-tool NOTES.md updates, a markdown-only session that this scope never loads. The FR-1.2b fence still catches output-swallowing, but the judgment rules "the fence cannot express" (stash -k with pre-commit, fsck before gc) now disappear in exactly the sessions that produced the defect. This is a floor-adjacent guard (FR-1.2b is in floor_guards) weakened without a measurement, even though the no_rule_files arm exists to measure it first.
head/evals/tasks/review-recall/review-pr-11.yaml:1 — MEDIUM: the record tasks review-pr-11 … review-pr-18 (and audit-pr-11 … audit-pr-18) sit under the existing suites' include glob (`tasks/review-recall/**/*.yaml`; the audit suite is presumably the same). Every plain run-eval.sh run of the suites, including the cycle-124 classic A/B and its baselines, therefore picks up 8 more fixtures with 3600 s timeouts and labels that may still be `approved: false`. Only run-arms.sh enforces the approval gate; run-eval.sh does not. That changes the classic A/B's composition and bypasses the "unapproved labels are not graded" rule the README states. Keep the record tasks out of the default include (e.g. the .yml trick used for review-kind-01, or a separate suite), or enforce approval in run-eval.sh.
head/evals/harness/compare-ab.py:155 — LOW: a control-arm comparison drops the "different prompt trees" rule and relies on source_commit agreement instead. But `set(A) != set(B)` is False when neither side recorded any source_commit (rows from an older run-eval, or a hand-built results dir). Two arms with distinct arm ids on different, unpinned trees then validate as a control comparison. Require a non-empty, single, shared source_commit (or identical prompt_tree_sha) when `control` is true.
head/evals/harness/compare-ab.py:71 — LOW: every model in `models_used` with output > 0 now counts as executor-model skew, here and in arms-report.py:144. execute-agent.sh:349 pins only CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL. The CLI's small/fast background model (ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL / the default Haiku model) is not pinned. Any trial where the CLI makes an auxiliary call makes the comparison invalid (exit 2) and every arm verdict "inconclusive (model skew)". Pin the background model too, or report auxiliary models separately from the executor.
head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:314 — LOW: is_transport_failure greps agent-output.json, which holds the model's final review text, for `network|socket hang up|5[0-9][0-9] |rate.?limit`. If the agent fails (exit 1) after writing text that mentions networking or an HTTP 5xx status, the failure is classified as transport, retried after --retry-wait, and recorded as transport_error instead of agent_error. Restrict the grep to stderr and to the result event's error fields.
head/tools/cycle-ratio.sh:100 — LOW: the kind counter matches `kind: <value>` on the raw line without stripping inline code spans, and it does not reject lines carrying two tokens. validate-artifact.sh validate_sprint_kinds strips code spans and rejects double tokens. The header (lines 13-14) claims "the same scope validate-artifact.sh --type sprint enforces", but a task ending in `` `kind: operator` `` is untagged for the validator and counted as operator here. Reuse the same awk (strip backtick spans, count tokens).
head/.claude/data/floor.yaml:10 — LOW: the comment says "Both bats suites pin this file's sha256". Only tests/unit/guard-origins.bats holds FLOOR_SHA256; floor-snapshot.bats has no pin and itself defers to guard-origins.bats. Since the comment documents the floor's tamper protection, it should be accurate.
head/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh:8 — LOW: the header says hooks yield "one row per unique script". The hooks table (render_hooks_block) and GY-8 emit one row per registration; write-mutation-logger.sh, for example, appears twice in hooks-reference.md. Fix the comment.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:408 — MEDIUM: rerunning a batch that already holds results is allowed (lines 251-256 accept it when source and model match), but collect() only appends to <arm>/results.jsonl and never truncates or dedupes it. A rerun (e.g. after a partial run) doubles every (fixture, arm, trial) row, while the per-batch DONE/FAILED counters restart at 0. arms-report.py pools every row, so coverage_gaps reads 6/3 trials and trial_means merges two runs under the same trial number. The pre-registered verdict is then computed on mixed, double-counted data. Either refuse a non-dry-run reuse of a batch that has results, or replace or skip rows already present.

head/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md:2 — MEDIUM: the new path scope (`**/*.sh`, `**/*.bats`, `.claude/scripts/**`, `.claude/hooks/**`) loads the stash rule only when shell sources are touched. The hazard is a git stash run from Bash during any skill. The incident the rule cites (#555, line 39) lost Edit-tool NOTES.md updates, a markdown-only session that this scope never loads. The FR-1.2b fence still catches output-swallowing, but the judgment rules "the fence cannot express" (stash -k with pre-commit, fsck before gc) now disappear in exactly the sessions that produced the defect. This is a floor-adjacent guard (FR-1.2b is in floor_guards) weakened without a measurement, even though the no_rule_files arm exists to measure it first.

-head/evals/tasks/review-recall/review-pr-11.yaml:1 — MEDIUM: the record tasks review-pr-11 … review-pr-18 (and audit-pr-11 … audit-pr-18) sit under the existing suites' include glob (`tasks/review-recall/**/*.yaml`; the audit suite is presumably the same). Every plain run-eval.sh run of the suites, including the cycle-124 classic A/B and its baselines, therefore picks up 8 more fixtures with 3600 s timeouts and labels that may still be `approved: false`. Only run-arms.sh enforces the approval gate; run-eval.sh does not. That changes the classic A/B's composition and bypasses the "unapproved labels are not graded" rule the README states. Keep the record tasks out of the default include (e.g. the .yml trick used for review-kind-01, or a separate suite), or enforce approval in run-eval.sh.

+head/evals/tasks/review-recall/review-pr-11.yaml:1 — MEDIUM: the record tasks review-pr-11 … review-pr-18 (and audit-pr-11 … audit-pr-18) sit under the existing suites' include glob (`tasks/review-recall/**/*.yaml` and `tasks/audit-recall/**/*.yaml`). Every plain run-eval.sh run of the suites, including the cycle-124 classic A/B and its baselines, therefore picks up 8 more fixtures with 3600 s timeouts and labels that may still be `approved: false`. Only run-arms.sh enforces the approval gate; run-eval.sh does not. That changes the classic A/B's composition and bypasses the "unapproved labels are not graded" rule the README states. Keep the record tasks out of the default include (e.g. the .yml trick used for review-kind-01, or a separate suite), or enforce approval in run-eval.sh.

head/evals/harness/compare-ab.py:155 — LOW: a control-arm comparison drops the "different prompt trees" rule and relies on source_commit agreement instead. But `set(A) != set(B)` is False when neither side recorded any source_commit (rows from an older run-eval, or a hand-built results dir). Two arms with distinct arm ids on different, unpinned trees then validate as a control comparison. Require a non-empty, single, shared source_commit (or identical prompt_tree_sha) when `control` is true.

head/evals/harness/compare-ab.py:71 — LOW: every model in `models_used` with output > 0 now counts as executor-model skew, here and in arms-report.py:144. execute-agent.sh:349 pins only CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL. The CLI's small/fast background model (ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL / the default Haiku model) is not pinned. Any trial where the CLI makes an auxiliary call makes the comparison invalid (exit 2) and every arm verdict "inconclusive (model skew)". Pin the background model too, or report auxiliary models separately from the executor.

head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:314 — LOW: is_transport_failure greps agent-output.json, which holds the model's final review text, for `network|socket hang up|5[0-9][0-9] |rate.?limit`. If the agent fails (exit 1) after writing text that mentions networking or an HTTP 5xx status, the failure is classified as transport, retried after --retry-wait, and recorded as transport_error instead of agent_error. Restrict the grep to stderr and to the result event's error fields.

I've written the review to `/workspace/review.md`. It has 11 findings and the verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**.

**Why it can't merge:**
- **A floor guard test always passes** (`tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats:39`). Test FS-2's jq filter uses `$in` before `$in` is defined, so jq won't compile it. I ran it: jq reports "$in is not defined" and exits 3. Both sides of the `diff` come out empty, and diff counts that as a match. The check meant to stop the FR-1.2b / FR-SZ* fence-corpus rows from changing never actually compares them.
- **One control arm can silently run as the baseline** (`evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:266`). If neither rule file is in the sandbox, the `rule_files` toggle still reports success. The PR's own docs say a toggle that can't take effect must fail the trial (exit 2), and the tests only cover that for the other two toggles.
- **Rerunning a batch double-counts trials** (`evals/harness/run-arms.sh:408`). Rerunning a batch with the same source and model is allowed, but results are only ever appended. The report then pools old and new rows, so trial counts and per-trial means are computed on duplicated data.
- **The stash-safety rule now rarely loads** (`.claude/rules/stash-safety.md:2`). It's now scoped to shell files only. The incident it comes from (#555) was a markdown-only session (NOTES.md edits), which the new scope never loads. That weakens a rule tied to a floor guard before the new control arm has measured the effect.
- **Record fixtures join the default suites** (`evals/tasks/review-recall/review-pr-11.yaml:1`). The new pr-11 … pr-18 tasks match the existing review-recall and audit-recall include globs. Ordinary `run-eval.sh` runs will pick them up, possibly with unapproved labels, because only `run-arms.sh` checks approval.

**Lower severity:**
- `compare-ab.py` accepts a control comparison where neither side recorded a source commit.
- Any auxiliary model output counts as executor-model skew, but only the subagent model is pinned. Any trial where the CLI's background model runs would void the comparison.
- The transport-failure check in `run-arms.sh` greps the agent's own review text, so a failed review that mentions networking gets retried as a transport error.
- `cycle-ratio.sh` counts task kinds differently from the validator it claims to match.
- Two comments are wrong: `floor.yaml:10` says two test suites pin its checksum (only one does), and `guard-yield.sh:8` describes the hooks table rows incorrectly.

**What I checked and found consistent:** the fence `@guard` markers match the origin map (I re-ran the script's marker check: all 34 fence ids match the map). The validator markers match their rows, the floor rows match `floor_guards`, and `floor.yaml` matches its pinned checksum.

**What I couldn't run:** `pr/` only contains the touched files, so the bats suites and `guard-yield.sh --check` can't run end to end here. The PR also doesn't include `grimoires/loa/guards.md` or the pr-11 … pr-18 fixture directories. That looks like the snapshot leaving them out (the PR's own seeding script skips `grimoires/`), so I didn't report them as missing.
